title: Research: twisted helper contract absorbs three R439 helper-star restorations into A (10,492 -> 10,489 on PR1188's word; no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Replacement-interface result with finite R439 instances. No new κ, and the
bit side does not bind.** This adds one registered package,
[`research/r439-twisted-star-absorption-seed02/`](research/r439-twisted-star-absorption-seed02/README.md).
No selected record, supplier, pinned file or `upstream/` changes.

**Twisted contract (card `bit-helper-contract`).** #1194's semantic-D contract
requires D to return every helper, `(x, y, h) -> (x, y + N h, h)`, and keeps the
literal-reverse cleanup H4. The twisted contract makes three changes:

- **H2-tw:** D may leave helpers twisted by an invertible, helper-only `T`,
  giving `(x, y + N h, T h)`. D stays frame-zero and source-free.
- **H4-tw:** C is z-only at the full frame and satisfies
  `C U' diag(I_x, T) = I`.
- **K-tw:** `N = K'T`.

H1, H3, H5 and `J = I` are kept.

- **Proof.** The block algebra gives the dirty boundary
  `(x, y, h) -> (x, y + x, h)` on every F2-module. Given the kept and structural
  clauses, the two equations are also necessary. The proof is in `PROOF.md`.
- **Two ways it weakens #1194.**
  - The cleanup is semantic even at `T = I`. #1311's stale-cleanup control
    satisfies it, which is why `PROOF.md` states that adopting H4-tw as a general
    interface needs a chronological bridge for non-literal cleanups.
  - The helpers may stay twisted.
- **The instances use neither relaxation's risk.** They keep the base words'
  literal C byte for byte and are bridged cut by cut.

**Helper-mixing word.** Delete a D restoration `a ^= b`. Replace the source set
`Sg` of an A gate that writes `a` before `a`'s first read with `Sg ⊕ S`, where
`S` is the unique register set whose current values sum to `b`'s column. This
preserves the boundary if and only if the new set is exactly `Sg ⊕ S`.

- **Exhaustive single-edge census.** On the #967, #1062, #1122 and #1188 words
  it finds exactly 48/48/48/47 positive moves. Of those, 45/45/45/44 are
  frame-illegal and **3** are frame-legal, and the 3 are the same on every word.
- **The three moves.** `506^=374` is absorbed at A[288] (substitute 69).
  `507^=355` is absorbed at A[290] (substitute 72). `514^=367` is absorbed at
  A[304] (substitute 360).

| | #1062 word | absorbed | #1188 word | absorbed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ADDs | 11,500 | **11,497** | 10,492 | **10,489** |
| F / B | 25,717 / 5,911,840 | 25,717 / 5,858,638 | 13,667 / 3,758,418 | 13,667 / 3,748,680 |
| bits (caps 104/192) | 95 / 182 | 95 / 182 | 91 / 175 | 91 / 175 |

Both absorbed words have:

- an exact dirty boundary on all 661 columns, forward and reverse, through the
  literal COPY/ERASE stream;
- identical per-register frame paths and exporter MOVE records;
- an unchanged paid profile, `{1:1323, 2:1342, 3:79, 4:44, 5:102, 6:11, 7:19}`,
  with rank mass 5,129.

The unchanged owner checker reports exactly four false flags:
`H2_D_frame0_targets_from_helpers`, `H4_C_literal_reverse_at_full`,
`K_equals_D` and `C_is_U_inverse`.

**Newly used premise.** The instances rely on the inherited common-frame /
climb-additivity premise, now applied to helpers. Targets already rely on it,
because they climb holding `y + N h`. #1194 confined its own substitution to
frame-zero prefixes. Here exactly three helpers (506, 507, 514) first climb out
of frame zero holding `centre + leaf`, at their absorbing gates.

**Not run.**
- Native 5/9/11-stage C++ replay. My open #1509 stand-in could enable it on
  hosts without Boost.
- Hosted emission and invoice, and outer assembly.

The census covers the single-edge, single-writer class only. It is not a global
minimum.

## Task and overlap

- **Base and track.** Base `0b1cccf8`. Seed 2 → bit supplier, card
  `bit-helper-contract` (catalogue priority revision 3), scope **refined**.
- **Lineage.**
  - #1194 (semantic-D contract, merged) and #1311 (its bridge on #1122's word).
  - #1580 and #1592 (open) exclude terminal restoration moves and compensation.
    This package's absorption comes before the first read and changes A, which
    answers #1592's stated next question for the centre-writer class.
- **Concurrent same-card work.** None of these leaves helpers twisted or
  absorbs a D restoration into A.
  - Larger scalar savings on the same #1062 word, by other mechanisms; whether
    they compose with these three absorptions is untested:
    - #1543: 11,489;
    - #1709: 11,488;
    - #1704: 11,380, under a different interface.
  - #1782 and #1805 work under #1194's restored-helper contract.
  - Discussion #1743's terminal-deferral claim expired without a PR.
- **Overlap searches** for absorb, twisted, cross-cut, `C_is_U_inverse`, H4,
  helper-star, restoration and helper contract, run at three points through
  12:20Z, found nothing on this mechanism.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-twisted-star-absorption-seed02 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-twisted-star-absorption-seed02
```

`verify.py` uses only the standard library and takes about 20 s. Its checks
raise `ValueError`, so they also run under `-O`; it is registered with and
without `-O`.

- **Inputs.** It pins all 7 inputs and runs the owner checker and exporter from
  the verified bytes.
- **Re-derivation.** It reruns the census on four words and rebuilds both
  absorbed words, requiring an exact match with the committed payloads.
- **Proof checks.** It checks the twisted identities and the per-cut
  chronology: at most 3 pending centres, each at frame zero until its absorbing
  gate.
- **Controls (16, all rejected or failing).**
  - Omitting the restorations without the A edit: a dirty-only counterexample.
  - The A edit with literal cleanup: fails on dirty helpers 506/507/514 and
    passes on clean ones.
  - Absorption after the first centre read.
  - A wrong substitute.
  - A frame-illegal substitution.
  - The #1194-style splice with #589's D, rejected with "helpers not restored".
  - A corrupted pin.
- **Perturbations.** 1,980 one-register perturbations per instance are all
  rejected.

It passes on Python 3.11–3.14.

**Pre-PR review.** A three-lens review found:
- **Verifier lens: "ship".** All data and code mutations were caught, and an
  independent re-implementation reproduced the census.
- **Proof lens:** confirmed the lemma by hand and with random circuits, plus the
  uniqueness, the criterion and the chronology. It corrected the
  "`T = I` recovers #1194" overclaim; the cleanup is weakened even at `T = I`,
  and that is now documented.
- **Claims lens:** all numbers, pins and credits check out. It added the
  concurrent-work section and fixed the notation.

- **Restoration-coalescing lineage:** #1155, #1199, #1203, #1205.

AI disclosure: prepared by Sagar Thakrar with substantial Anthropic Claude
assistance, including explorer, judge, builder and reviewer subagents. No
independent human review. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Multi-gate splits of `S`, and chaining the gain-0 moves.
2. Native replay of the absorbed words, with Boost or the #1509 stand-in.
3. Whether feedback or shear gains appear once the helper exit may be twisted
   (`T ≠ I`), complementing #1706.
4. Whether maintainers would adopt H4-tw, which would also need a bridge for
   non-literal cleanups.
